title: Adaptive GPU slab allocation and KV-eviction governance for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Nayar
description: Problem: Multi-tenant inference nodes are experiencing intermittent OOMs during mixed workloads where long sequences inflate KV allocations and transient batches spike activations. Current static split of GPU memory (weights / KV / activations) is inefficient: conservative reserves waste capacity, aggressive packing causes tail OOMs.
context_and_goal: Goal: Build an adaptive slab allocator that maintains a soft fractional budget for model weights, per-tenant KV cache, and activations, with a runtime controller that enforces graceful degradation when memory pressure approaches safety thresholds. We want: (1) predictable tail latency SLAs, (2) fewer OOM incidents, (3) measurable cost improvements by reclaiming unused KV headroom, and (4) an automated rollout path with simulator-backed safety checks.
approach_summary: 1) Introduce 'slab profiles' per node which define baseline fractions: weight_reserved, kv_soft_fraction, activation_soft_fraction. 2) Runtime telemetry exports exact per-tenant KV bytes, activation peaks, and estimated serialization overheads. 3) Controller runs periodic optimization (10s window) to reassign soft headroom between KV and activations based on recent quantiles (e.g., 95th/99th) and model weight footprints. 4) When predicted tail crosses safety margin, controller triggers eviction tiers: a) short-lived prefix eviction (noncritical KV entries), b) quantized KV eviction (store compacted representations), c) admission throttle (reject or reroute low-priority requests) as last resort. 5) Provide flags to enable simulation-first rollout and canary per-pool.
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Aggressive eviction reduces cache hit-rate and increases token-cost due to re-computation; need to measure delta via offline eval.
- Frequent rebalancing can add jitter to latency; use smoothing windows and rate-limits on reassignments.
- Some models have skewed KV growth (long chat histories) — need tenant-aware caps.
- For Dedicated customers, allow pinning of hard fractions vs. hosted where controller is fully automated.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator: end-to-end simulation shows >=50% reduction in OOMs on historical mixed-workload traces compared to static split
Telemetry: new metrics emitted (kv_reserved_bytes, kv_eviction_count, activation_peak_bytes, slab_rebalance_events) and surfaced in Console dashboards
Safety: Canary rollout on 5% of serving pools with rollback if OOM rate increases >10% relative to baseline
Performance: 95th latency regression <= 5% for canary pools after enabling adaptive allocator
Docs: Runbook and playbook added to Confluence with exact undo steps and failure modes
